name: Frame
purpose: Own responsive logical size constraints for one local element without taking over layout, paint, spacing, or overflow.
useWhen: A rail, copy region, media canvas, or scroll boundary needs an explicit inline or block size constraint.

avoidWhen.condition: The need is shared page measure, child arrangement, paint, aspect ratio, or scrolling.
avoidWhen.useInstead: Container, Stack/Grid, Surface, AspectRatio, or ScrollArea

composition: Use Frame inside a layout Item, or let Stack.Item/Grid.Item compose asChild around Frame when one host must own both parent participation and internal constraints.
For bounded long content, put ScrollArea inside a maxBlockSize Frame; Frame constrains and ScrollArea scrolls.

rules.statement: Use Frame only for inlineSize, minInlineSize, maxInlineSize, blockSize, minBlockSize, or maxBlockSize.
Prefer logical size constraints and responsive values rather than physical width/height application classes.
Keep flex/grid participation on Stack.Item or Grid.Item; Frame owns the constrained element's internal geometry.
Use nested Frames when separate ancestors need separate constraints; each Frame keeps its base and responsive values locally scoped.
Do not treat maxBlockSize as scrolling; compose ScrollArea when overflow must remain reachable.
Load styles.css or core.css plus frame.css.

commonMistakes.mistake: Turning Frame into a universal Box with paint, spacing, position, overflow, and typography props.
commonMistakes.correction: Keep Frame to six logical constraints and compose the existing Brick owner for every other responsibility.

validation: Check responsive carry-forward, zoom/reflow, long content, RTL, vertical writing, and focus visibility.
Confirm every constrained node has one clear job and that ScrollArea owns any required overflow.
